question: What do fungus-farming ants carry on their own bodies to keep a crop-killing mould out of their gardens?
answer: Bacteria that make antibiotics. Currie and colleagues found leafcutter and other fungus-farming ants carrying filamentous bacteria in whitish crusts on their cuticle. The bacteria produce compounds that suppress Escovopsis, a parasitic mould that attacks only the ants' fungus gardens. Remove the bacteria and the gardens were overrun. The farmers carry their fungicide on their backs.
move: Any farm run long enough ends up farming its own defences.
reference: Currie, Scott, Summerbell & Malloch, Fungus-growing ants use antibiotic-producing bacteria to control garden parasites, Nature, 1999
